articles.title: Mechanical Execution of Work
articles.text: Electrical equipment shall be installed in a neat and workmanlike manner.

articles.title: Electrical Connections
articles.text: Because of different characteristics of dissimilar metals, devices such as pressure terminal or pressure splicing connectors and soldering lugs shall be identified for the material of the conductor and shall be properly installed and used.

articles.title: Terminals
articles.text: Connection of conductors to terminal parts shall ensure a thoroughly good connection without damaging the conductors and shall be made by means of pressure connectors, solder lugs, or splices to flexible leads.

articles.title: Working Space - Minimum Clear Distances
articles.text: The depth of the working space in the direction of live parts shall not be less than that specified in Table 110.26(A)(1) unless the requirements of 110.26(A)(1)(a) or (A)(1)(b) are met.

articles.title: Working Space - Width
articles.text: The width of the working space in front of the electrical equipment shall be the width of the equipment or 30 inches, whichever is greater.

articles.title: Working Space - Height
articles.text: The working space shall be clear and extend from the grade, floor, or platform to a height of 6-1/2 feet or the height of the equipment, whichever is greater.

articles.title: GFCI Protection - Dwelling Units
articles.text: All 125-volt through 250-volt receptacles installed in the locations specified in 210.8(A)(1) through (A)(11) shall have ground-fault circuit-interrupter protection for personnel.

articles.title: GFCI Protection - Bathrooms
articles.text: All 125-volt through 250-volt receptacles in bathrooms of dwelling units shall have GFCI protection.

articles.title: GFCI Protection - Garages and Accessory Buildings
articles.text: All 125-volt through 250-volt receptacles in garages and accessory buildings with floors at or below grade level shall have GFCI protection.

articles.title: GFCI Protection - Kitchens
articles.text: All 125-volt through 250-volt receptacles that serve countertop surfaces in kitchens of dwelling units shall have GFCI protection.

articles.title: GFCI Protection - Laundry Areas
articles.text: All 125-volt through 250-volt receptacles in laundry areas of dwelling units shall have GFCI protection.

articles.title: Branch Circuits Required - Bathroom
articles.text: In addition to the number of branch circuits required by other parts of this section, at least one 120-volt, 20-ampere branch circuit shall be provided to supply bathroom receptacle outlet(s).

articles.title: Branch Circuits Required - Laundry
articles.text: In addition to the number of branch circuits required by other parts of this section, at least one 120-volt, 20-ampere branch circuit shall be provided to supply the laundry receptacle outlet(s).

articles.title: Branch Circuits Required - Kitchen Small Appliance
articles.text: In addition to the number of branch circuits required by other parts of this section, two or more 20-ampere small-appliance branch circuits shall be provided for kitchen receptacle outlets.

articles.title: AFCI Protection - Dwelling Units
articles.text: All 120-volt, single-phase, 15- and 20-ampere branch circuits supplying outlets and devices installed in dwelling unit kitchens, family rooms, dining rooms, living rooms, parlors, libraries, dens, bedrooms, sunrooms, recreation rooms, closets, hallways, laundry areas, and similar rooms or areas shall be protected by any of the means described in 210.12(A)(1) through (A)(6).

articles.title: Receptacle Outlets Required - General
articles.text: In every kitchen, family room, dining room, living room, parlor, library, den, sunroom, bedroom, recreation room, or similar room or area of dwelling units, receptacle outlets shall be installed so that no point measured horizontally along the floor line of any wall space is more than 6 feet from a receptacle outlet.

articles.title: Receptacle Outlets Required - Small Appliance
articles.text: In the kitchen, pantry, breakfast room, dining room, or similar area of a dwelling unit, the two or more 20-ampere small-appliance branch circuits required by 210.11(C)(3) shall serve all wall and floor receptacle outlets covered by 210.52(A), all countertop outlets covered by 210.52(C), and receptacle outlets for refrigeration equipment.

articles.title: Receptacle Outlets Required - Countertops
articles.text: In kitchens, pantries, breakfast rooms, dining rooms, and similar areas of dwelling units, receptacle outlets for countertop spaces shall be installed so that no point along the wall line is more than 24 inches measured horizontally from a receptacle outlet in that space.

articles.title: Lighting Loads for Specified Occupancies
articles.text: A unit load of not less than that specified in Table 220.12 for occupancies specified therein shall constitute the minimum lighting load.

articles.title: General Calculations - Services and Feeders
articles.text: The computed load of a feeder or service shall not be less than the sum of the loads on the branch circuits supplied, as determined by Part II of this article, after any applicable demand factors permitted by Part III or IV have been applied.

articles.title: Optional Calculation - Dwelling Unit
articles.text: An optional calculation for a one-family dwelling or an individual dwelling unit of a two-family dwelling or a multifamily dwelling shall be permitted in accordance with Table 220.82.

articles.title: Service Disconnect - Location
articles.text: The service disconnecting means shall be installed at a readily accessible location either outside of a building or structure or inside nearest the point of entrance of the service conductors.

articles.title: Rating of Service Disconnecting Means
articles.text: The service disconnecting means shall have a rating not less than the calculated load to be served.

articles.title: Protection of Conductors
articles.text: Conductors, other than flexible cords, flexible cables, and fixture wires, shall be protected against overcurrent in accordance with their ampacities.

articles.title: Small Conductors
articles.text: Unless specifically permitted in 240.4(E) or 240.4(G), the overcurrent protection shall not exceed 15 amperes for 14 AWG, 20 amperes for 12 AWG, and 30 amperes for 10 AWG copper; or 15 amperes for 12 AWG and 25 amperes for 10 AWG aluminum and copper-clad aluminum.

articles.title: Overcurrent Device Location - Accessibility
articles.text: Overcurrent devices shall be readily accessible and shall be installed so that the center of the grip of the operating handle of the switch or circuit breaker, when in its highest position, is not more than 6 feet 7 inches above the floor or working platform.

articles.title: General Requirements - Grounding of Electrical Systems
articles.text: Electrical systems that are grounded shall be connected to earth in a manner that will limit the voltage imposed by lightning, line surges, or unintentional contact with higher-voltage lines and that will stabilize the voltage to earth during normal operation.

articles.title: Grounding Electrode Conductor Connection
articles.text: A grounding electrode conductor shall be used to connect the equipment grounding conductors, the service-equipment enclosures, and, where the system is grounded, the grounded conductor to the grounding electrode(s).

articles.title: Grounding Electrode System
articles.text: All grounding electrodes as described in 250.52(A)(1) through (A)(7) that are present at each building or structure served shall be bonded together to form the grounding electrode system.

articles.title: Grounding Electrodes - Metal Underground Water Pipe
articles.text: A metal underground water pipe in direct contact with the earth for 10 feet or more, including any metal well casing that is bonded to the pipe and that is in direct contact with the earth.

articles.title: Grounding Electrodes - Ground Rod
articles.text: Rod-type grounding electrodes of stainless steel, copper, or zinc coated steel shall be at least 8 feet in length and 5/8 inch in diameter.

articles.title: Grounding Electrode Conductor Installation - Aluminum
articles.text: Bare aluminum or copper-clad aluminum grounding electrode conductors shall not be used where in direct contact with masonry or the earth or where subject to corrosive conditions.

articles.title: Bonding of Piping Systems - Metal Water Piping
articles.text: The metal water piping system shall be bonded to the service equipment enclosure, the grounded conductor at the service, the grounding electrode conductor where of sufficient size, or to the one or more grounding electrodes used.

articles.title: Size of Equipment Grounding Conductors
articles.text: Equipment grounding conductors of the wire type shall not be smaller than shown in Table 250.122.

articles.title: Conductor Ampacities
articles.text: Ampacities for conductors shall be as specified in Table 310.16 through Table 310.21 and their accompanying notes.

articles.title: Ampacities of Insulated Conductors
articles.text: Table 310.16 provides allowable ampacities of insulated conductors rated up to and including 2000 volts, based on ambient temperature of 30 degrees C.

articles.title: NM Cable - Uses Permitted
articles.text: Type NM, NMC, and NMS cables shall be permitted to be used in one- and two-family dwellings and their attached or detached garages and storage buildings, and in multifamily dwellings.

articles.title: NM Cable - Securing and Supporting
articles.text: Nonmetallic-sheathed cable shall be supported and secured by staples, cable ties, straps, hangers, or similar fittings at intervals not exceeding 4-1/2 feet and within 12 inches of every cabinet, box, or fitting.

articles.title: Receptacle Replacements - GFCI
articles.text: Where a grounding means does not exist in the receptacle enclosure, the installation of a GFCI receptacle or a GFCI circuit breaker shall be permitted.

articles.title: Receptacles in Damp or Wet Locations
articles.text: A receptacle installed outdoors in a location protected from the weather or in other damp locations shall have an enclosure for the receptacle that is weatherproof when the receptacle cover(s) are closed.

articles.title: Receptacles in Wet Locations
articles.text: A receptacle installed in a wet location shall have an enclosure that is weatherproof whether or not the attachment plug cap is inserted.

articles.title: Circuit Directory or Circuit Identification
articles.text: Every circuit and circuit modification shall be legibly identified as to its clear, evident, and specific purpose or use. The identification shall include an approved degree of detail that allows each circuit to be distinguished from all others.

articles.title: Overcurrent Protection of Panelboards
articles.text: In addition to the requirement of 408.30, a panelboard shall be provided with physical means to prevent the installation of more overcurrent devices than that number for which the panelboard was designed, rated, and listed.

articles.title: Luminaires in Specific Locations - Wet or Damp
articles.text: Luminaires installed in wet or damp locations shall be installed so that water cannot enter or accumulate in wiring compartments, lampholders, or other electrical parts.

articles.title: Appliances - Flexible Cords
articles.text: Flexible cord shall be permitted for connection of appliances to facilitate their frequent interchange or to prevent the transmission of noise or vibration.

articles.title: Motor Ampere Ratings - Table Values
articles.text: Where the current rating of a motor is used to determine the ampacity of conductors, switches, branch-circuit short-circuit and ground-fault protection, and the motor overload protection, Table 430.247, Table 430.248, Table 430.249, and Table 430.250 shall be used.

articles.title: Motor Branch-Circuit Short-Circuit and Ground-Fault Protection
articles.text: The motor branch-circuit short-circuit and ground-fault protective device shall comply with 430.52(B) and either 430.52(C) or (D). The rating or setting of the device shall not exceed the values given in Table 430.52.

articles.title: Pool Area Lighting - Luminaire Height
articles.text: Luminaires, lighting outlets, and ceiling-suspended fans shall not be installed over the pool or over the area extending 5 feet horizontally from the inside walls of a pool unless they are at least 12 feet above the maximum water level.

articles.title: Equipotential Bonding
articles.text: An equipotential bonding grid shall comply with the requirements of 680.26(A) and (B).

articles.title: GFCI Protection - Outdoors
articles.text: All 125-volt through 250-volt receptacles installed outdoors of dwelling units shall have GFCI protection. This includes receptacles on porches, patios, decks, and attached garages with direct outdoor access.

articles.title: GFCI Protection - Bathtubs and Shower Stalls
articles.text: All 125-volt through 250-volt receptacles installed within 6 feet of the outside edge of a bathtub or shower stall shall have GFCI protection.

articles.title: GFCI Protection - Specific Appliances
articles.text: GFCI protection shall be provided for dishwashers in dwelling unit locations. The branch circuit supplying the dishwasher shall be protected by a listed GFCI device.

articles.title: AFCI Protection - Branch Circuit Extensions or Modifications
articles.text: Where branch-circuit wiring is modified, replaced, or extended in any of the areas specified in 210.12(A), the branch circuit shall be protected by one of the means described in 210.12(A)(1) through (A)(6).

articles.title: Receptacle Outlets - Island and Peninsular Countertop Spaces
articles.text: At least one receptacle outlet shall be provided at each island countertop space with a long dimension of 24 inches or greater and a short dimension of 12 inches or greater. At least one receptacle outlet shall be provided at each peninsular countertop space with a long dimension of 24 inches or greater and a short dimension of 12 inches or greater.

articles.title: Receptacle Outlets - Bathrooms
articles.text: At least one receptacle outlet shall be installed within 36 inches of the outside edge of each basin. The receptacle outlet shall be located on a wall or partition that is adjacent to the basin or basin countertop, or installed on the side or face of the basin cabinet not more than 12 inches below the countertop.

articles.title: Receptacle Outlets - Outdoor Outlets for Dwelling Units
articles.text: For a one-family dwelling and each unit of a two-family dwelling that is at grade level, at least two receptacle outlets accessible while standing at grade level and not more than 6-1/2 feet above grade shall be installed at the front and back of the dwelling.

articles.title: Receptacle Outlets - Basements, Garages, and Accessory Buildings
articles.text: For a one-family dwelling, at least one receptacle outlet shall be installed in each attached garage and in each detached garage or accessory building with electric power. At least one receptacle outlet shall be installed in an unfinished area of the basement in addition to any laundry area receptacles.

articles.title: Next Higher Standard Overcurrent Device
articles.text: Where the standard ratings in 240.6(A) do not correspond with the ampacity of the conductors being protected, the next higher standard overcurrent device rating shall be permitted to be used, provided the conductors being protected are not part of a branch circuit supplying more than one receptacle for cord-and-plug-connected portable loads.

articles.title: NM Cable - Ampacity
articles.text: Where more than two NM cables containing two or more current-carrying conductors are installed through the same opening in wood framing without maintaining spacing, the ampacity of each conductor shall be adjusted in accordance with Table 310.15(C)(1). The adjustment factors shall apply only to the number of current-carrying conductors.

articles.title: General Lighting Demand Factors
articles.text: The demand factors specified in Table 220.42 shall apply to the portion of the total branch-circuit load computed for general illumination. The demand factors shall not apply to the portion of the total branch-circuit load computed for heavy-duty lampholders. For dwelling units, the first 3,000 VA at 100%, the next 3,001 to 120,000 VA at 35%, and the remainder over 120,000 VA at 25%.

articles.title: Small-Appliance and Laundry Loads - Dwelling Unit
articles.text: In each dwelling unit, the load shall be computed at 1,500 VA for each 2-wire small-appliance branch circuit required by 210.11(C)(1) and each laundry branch circuit required by 210.11(C)(2). These loads shall be permitted to be included with the general lighting load and subjected to the demand factors in Table 220.42.

articles.title: Electric Dryer Load - Dwelling Unit
articles.text: The load for household electric clothes dryers in a dwelling unit shall be either 5,000 watts or the nameplate rating, whichever is larger, for each dryer served. The demand factors in Table 220.54 shall be permitted for the number of dryers served.

articles.title: Electric Cooking Equipment - Dwelling Unit
articles.text: The demand load for household electric ranges, wall-mounted ovens, counter-mounted cooking units, and other household cooking appliances individually rated in excess of 1-3/4 kW shall be permitted to be computed according to Table 220.55. A single branch circuit serving a household cooking appliance rated at not more than 12 kW shall have a maximum demand of 8 kW.

articles.title: Optional Calculation - Existing Dwelling Unit
articles.text: An optional calculation for an existing dwelling unit shall be permitted. The total load of the dwelling unit shall be determined by adding the general lighting and receptacle load, the small-appliance and laundry load, and any additional nameplate loads. Apply a demand factor of 100% to the first 10 kVA and 40% to the remainder.

articles.title: Supplemental Electrode Required
articles.text: A single rod, pipe, or plate electrode shall be supplemented by an additional electrode of a type specified in 250.52(A)(2) through (A)(8). The supplemental electrode shall be permitted to be bonded to the rod, pipe, or plate electrode, the grounding electrode conductor, the grounded service-entrance conductor, or the service equipment enclosure. Exception: If a single rod, pipe, or plate grounding electrode has a resistance to earth of 25 ohms or less, the supplemental electrode shall not be required.

articles.title: Intersystem Bonding Termination
articles.text: An intersystem bonding termination for connecting intersystem bonding conductors required for other systems shall be provided external to enclosures at the service equipment or metering equipment enclosure and at the disconnecting means for any additional buildings or structures. The intersystem bonding termination shall consist of a set of terminals with the capacity for connection of not less than three intersystem bonding conductors.
